newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-SOUTH AFRICA LIKELY TO STRUGGLE IF THEY MAKE FRANCE '98.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SOUTH AFRICA LIKELY TO STRUGGLE IF THEY MAKE FRANCE '98.

text.p: England and South Africa who met in a full international for the first time on Saturday, could well meet again in the World Cup finals next year -- but one thing seems certain if they do.
The game would be in the early stages of the competition because on Saturday's evidence South Africa look unlikely to make a major impact in France '98.

England's prospects cannot be judged on the basis of Saturday's unimpressive 2-1 win at Old Trafford because manager Glenn Hoddle fielded what amounted to a reserve side with eight changes from the team that beat Georgia in their last World Cup qualifer in April.
Both countries still have to qualify for France '98 and the participation of neither is certain.

Both face important qualifying matches soon -- England go to Poland for a make-or-break group two qualifier in Chorzow next Saturday while South Africa, the African champions, should qualify if they beat Zambia and Congo at home in their remaining two qualifiers.

But their qualification has been thrown into doubt even if they win their group. The political upheavals in Zaire, now renamed the Democratic Republic of the Congo, could have repercussions for South Africa if the new government in that central African country decide to withdraw from the World Cup.

If that happens, South Africa could lose the points they gained in home and away victories over Zaire, falling from first place to bottom in their group. It would then be up to FIFA to settle the issue.
South African coach Clive Barker was pleased with his team's performance on Saturday, even though they failed to make any impression on the England defence throughout the second half.
"We thoroughly enjoyed the occasion despite the result" he said.

The most contentious moment of a one-sided match came in the last few seconds when substitute Linda Buthelezi scythed down Paul Gascoigne from behind, leaving the England midfielder's fitness in doubt for the match in Poland.
The injury.at first rumoured to be a broken leg, was later diagnosed as a badly bruised calf which would be given 48 hours of intensive treatment.
Hoddle, hoping the problematic Gascoigne would use this warm-up to prove his fitness for Chorzow, was angry afterwards, accusing the South African of a rash challenge.
But Barker said: "There was no malice. Buthelezi was just over-enthusiastic. We went to see Paul and hope he will be fit for the Poland game but we won't apologise because that is part of football."

While Lazio defender Mark Fish, who turned down the chance to play regularly at Old Trafford for Manchester United when he opted for Italy instead, had a superb match and Doctor Khumalo and John "Shoes" Mosheou displayed some wonderful ball skills, South Africa never put England under any sustained pressure.
They probably would not have scored if England goalkeeper Nigel Martyn had not fumbled a save which led to Philomen Masinga's equaliser just before half-time.
England took the lead through Robert Lee in the 20th minute and won the match when Ian Wright scored his first England goal for four years with 15 minutes to play.
